stem:
The average velocity of gas molecules is 400 m/sec calculate its
r.m.s. velocity at the same temperature
solution:
$U_{av} = \sqrt{\frac{8RT}{\pi M}}$ and
$U_{rms} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$
$\therefore\frac{U_{av}}{U_{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{8RT}{\pi M}} \times \sqrt{\frac{M}{3RT}} = \sqrt{\frac{8}{3\pi}} = 0.9216$
or $U_{av} = 0.9216 \times U_{rms}$
Given $U_{av} = 400m/s$
$U_{rms} = \frac{400}{0.9216} = 434.02m/s$

stem:
An aqueous solution contains
${Hg}^{2 +},{Hg}_{2}^{2 +},{Pb}^{2 +}{Ag}^{+},{Bi}^{3 +}$ and
${Cd}^{2 +}$. Out of these, how many ions will produce white precipitate
with dilute HCl?
solution:
${Pb}^{2 +} + 2{Cl}^{-} \longrightarrow {PbCl}_{2} \downarrow (\ white\ );{Hg}_{2^{2 +}} + 2{Cl}^{-} \longrightarrow {Hg}_{2}{Cl}_{2} \downarrow (\ white\ )$
${Ag}^{+} + {Cl}^{-} \longrightarrow AgCl \downarrow \ (white)\ $
$K_{sp}$ of chlorides of ${Pb}^{2 +}$ and ${Hg}_{2}^{2 +}$is low as
compared to $K_{sp}$ of ${Hg}^{2 +}$ and ${Cd}^{2 +}$. Chloride ion
concentration provided by dilute HCl is just enough to exceed the
$K_{sp}$ of ${PbCl}_{2}$ and ${Hg}_{2}{Cl}_{2}$. Thus ${Pb}^{2 +}$ and
${Hg}_{2}^{2 +}$ are precipitated as their chlorides.

stem: The set with correct order of acidity is
options:
HClO < HClO2 < HClO3 < HClO4
(B) HClO4 < HClO3 < HClO2 < HClO
solution:
According to conjugate acid-base theory, that acid is more
acidic whose conjugate base is more stable. The order of the stability
of the conjugate bases of these acids is as follows:
ClO- < ClO2- < ClO3- < ClO4- on the basis of the charge
dispersion on the oxygen atoms (more charge dispersion on oxygen
atoms, more stable is the conjugate base). Also, for oxyacids of same
element, as oxidation state of element increases, acidic strength of
oxyacids increases.
